artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: New pure module (no I/O, no client=). article_rows(publisher_code, body_bytes, received_form, bronze_key, fetched_at, retrieval_mode, run_stamp, discovery=None) extracts the vendor object per publisher (SA data.attributes/relationships/included, Bloomberg story, Barron's articleData+body, WSJ's whole pageProps, FT's JSON-LD articleBody object, or the record itself for received_form=normalised_record), keeps every field, retypes only TIMESTAMP_FIELDS-named top-level fields, derives the published_utc/published_offset_min/published_date_utc/published_precision clock, and adds article_key/publisher/article_id/title/text_blocks/bronze_key/fetched_at/retrieval_mode/run_stamp plus the optional discovery columns. listing_hit_rows(...) does the same per listing/search bronze body, one row per hit with 1-based search_rank, carrying query_sha256/fetch_date_utc/search_page/source for the record key. retrieval_mode is refused via ValueError outside {backfill, live}.

New file, exactly the 14 arms section 1 item 4 names, over an in-process STUB S3 client (same shape as lib/research/harvest/tests/test_store.py). Each 'every field' arm flattens the fixture's own vendor object (a *_vendor() helper mirroring the module's own extraction) and the produced row, and asserts the missing/mismatched leaf list is empty. test_partition_is_fetch_date_not_published_date and test_uploader_silver_reads_bronze_not_record exercise the REAL lib/research/harvest/store.py functions (silver_append, silver_latest) against the stub client, never a re-implementation. No network, no vendor call, no live bucket.

HarvestUploader.run gains retrieval_mode='live' (default), threaded into _run_articles and _run_listings. _run_articles builds its silver row via silver_from_bronze.article_rows(publisher, payload, "as_received", bronze_key, fetched_at, retrieval_mode, run_stamp) from the SAME bytes just put as bronze -- never harvest_grammar.article_silver_row(record, bronze_key) (removed from this path; the function itself is left in place for other callers). received_form is hardcoded "as_received" here (no per-row column exists yet in harvest_raw_outbox; HVST-h-9 adds normalised_record rows later). _run_listings now also puts bronze via put_listing_bronze THEN appends listing_hit rows via silver_from_bronze.listing_hit_rows with record key (query_sha256, fetch_date_utc, search_page, search_rank, source).
